Other pharmacological approaches to the activation of brown adipose tissue
Products that have been proposed to stimulate BAT activity through means other than the activation of the adrenergic sympathetic
pathway include capsaicinoids, the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist exenatide, the dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP4)

inhibitor sitagliptin and secretin. Capsaicinoids are alkaloid found in chili peppers that are thought to enhance energy expenditure
when ingested. Capsaicinoid analogs, known as capsinoids, have been found to be able to activate BAT, and the combination of
capsinoids with cold exposure has a synergistic effect on BAT development. This suggests the activation of BAT by cold exposure
can be enhanced by the consumption of capsinoids.
Stimulation of the GLP-1R receptor was found to enhance BAT thermogenesis in mice. In humans, the GLP-1R agonist exenatide
was found to have no effect on energy expenditure in obese individuals. However, exenatide has an anorexic effect that could lead to
a decrease in energy expenditure in the short term, which could obfuscate potential increases in BAT thermogenesis. Following this
